text:
Anya (Product): ok folks — quick sync. I need alignment on the long-term platform trajectory: routing policies, multi-region SLAs, and tenant isolation. We have customer asks that push for per-tenant regional locks + strict data residency. what are the realistic gating criteria for a Q4 pilot?
Sam (Eng): rough take: core pieces = routing policy DSL, tenancy metadata, and cross-region failover. each is doable but scoped. biggest unknown = state migration/evacuation path for slices.
Lina (Architecture): +1. propose launch gates: (1) policy DSL v1 with test harness, (2) per-region capacity accounting, (3) graceful evacuation test w/ <500ms tail increase, (4) automated fallback to cold model variant.
Mike (Sales): customer ask: one enterprise (EU fintech) requires region-lock + audit logs before we can sign. they want a firm timeline — can we give them a pilot window?
Zoe (Customer Success): if we promise a pilot we need docs + runbook for cutover and rollback. CS will own runbook but needs eng to own the playbook steps. also we should list user-visible limits up-front.
Sam (Eng): implementation notes: policy DSL v1 could be a config-first system (yaml) that maps tenants -> region preference + fallback chain. pairing it with a routing engine is ~6w for a small team. evacuation tooling another 4w.
Dan (Eng Infra): infra constraints: cross-region KV syncing is the hard part. either accept eventual consistency for tenant metadata or build a coordination service. coordination adds operational surface and SLO risk.
Lina (Architecture): tradeoffs: stronger isolation (synchronous metadata) increases latency and failure surface. alternative: soft affinity + strong ingress filtering + SLA tiers. we can tier customers: Gold = strict region pinning (higher cost), Bronze = best-effort.
Anya (Product): that tiering approach seems promising — gives sales something to sell and sets realistic expectations. Mike, can you validate pricing appetite for a premium isolation tier?
Mike (Sales): yes — most will pay for guaranteed isolation. need a baseline unit price and commitment term. I can sketch numbers after chat with finance.
Zoe (Customer Success): ops note: any isolation tier must include an incident playbook and a post-mortem template specific to region cutovers. otherwise CS gets paged constantly.
Sam (Eng): proposal: milestone plan for pilot (8–12w): week 1–2: DSL + config schema; week 3–6: routing engine & policy enforcement; week 7: evacuation simulate; week 8: docs + runbook + pilot signups.
Lina (Architecture): add acceptance tests: simulated regional outage (packet loss + delayed KV), tenant traffic reroute under load, and a regression eval against model variants. must define SLO bump thresholds.
Anya (Product): launch criteria draft: 1) policy DSL + tests green, 2) two pilot customers onboarded, 3) evacuation <X% error delta (TBD), 4) runbook + monitoring dashboards live.
Dan (Eng Infra): monitoring requirements: per-tenant latencies, region affinity metrics, KV staleness histogram, and an automated alert when affinity broken >1% of requests.
Mike (Sales): FYI we have another customer (MSP) asking for tenant slices per region for compliance. they want multi-tenant shielding per slice. sounds similar but might need stronger telemetry for audits.
Anya (Product): action items: - Sam & Lina: create a short RFC with the DSL sketch + migration constraints by Fri. - Dan: list infra risks and potential mitigations. - Mike & Zoe: identify two pilot customers and confirm commitments.
Sam (Eng): will do RFC. I'll include a minimal yaml example and an evacuation runbook draft.
Lina (Architecture): i'll add possible fallback strategies and a matrix for consistency vs latency tradeoffs.
Dan (Eng Infra): i'll write up KV options (eventual vs coord) + rough cost estimate.
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: infra-canary -> staging at 2024-07-18T10:00Z :rocket:
Zoe (Customer Success): I'll reach out to EU fintech and MSP this week to gauge timelines.
Anya (Product): cool — let's aim to reconvene next Tue after RFCs. please drop any blockers in this thread. :thumbsup:
Sam (Eng): one blocker: we need a stable perf benchmark for model cold vs quantized fallbacks. Lina, can you recommend an eval harness?
Lina (Architecture): use the existing perf runner from eng-ml, add a region-emulation layer. i'll sync with @eng-ml to get a baseline.
Mike (Sales): note for timeline: procurement cycles mean pilot might slip. flagging that as risk.
Anya (Product): noted. thanks all. I'll capture the launch criteria and post a short PRD after the RFCs land.
